articleTitle: NAS-Based Recursive Stage Partial Network (Rspnet) for Light-Weight Semantic Segmentation
abstract: Current NAS-based semantic segmentation methods focus on accuracy improvements rather than light weight design. In this paper, we propose a two-stage framework to design our NAS-based RSPNet model for light-weight semantic segmentation. The first architecture search determines the inner cell structure, and the second architecture search considers exponentially growing paths to finalize the outer structure of the network. It was shown in the literature that the fusion of high- and low-resolution feature maps produces stronger representations. To find the expected macro structure without manual design, we adopt a new path-attention mechanism to efficiently search for suitable paths to fuse useful information for better segmentation. Our search for repeatable micro-structures from cells leads to a superior network architecture in semantic segmentation. In addition, we propose an RSP (recursive Stage Partial) architecture to search a light-weight design for NAS-based semantic segmentation. The light-weight NAS architecture with only 1/4 parameter size of SoTA architectures can achieve SoTA performance on semantic segmentation on the Cityscapes dataset without using any backbones.

articleTitle: Building an Observable System Based on OpenTelemetry
abstract: In traditional monitoring systems, the health status of services is typically assessed through metrics and logs. However, as the scope of monitoring expands from a monolithic architecture to a distributed system composed of multiple services or more granular microservices, traditional monitoring systems struggle to effectively pinpoint specific errors and their root causes. We propose an observability framework based on OpenTelemetry to generate trace data that captures contextual information and event correlations of requests thereby extending the existing monitoring system into an observability system. The study leverages a Hook to implement instrumentation in a PHP environment, ensuring minimal intrusiveness. Additionally, it traces intra-service function calls and inter-service requests to provide a thorough understanding of the execution path of requests.

articleTitle: Segmentation of aortic valve area and detection of hinge points using two-step nested U-Net
abstract: Aortic stenosis (AS) is a prevalent cardiac valve disease among the elderly, with a significant impact on individuals aged 75 and older. Traditionally, surgical aortic valve replacement (SAVR) has been the primary treatment for AS, but the advent of transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) has offered a minimally invasive alternative, particularly beneficial for high-risk patients. The success of TAVI relies heavily on preoperative evaluation, including precise anatomical measurements and imaging characteristics. This study aims to develop and validate a deep learning model to automate the detection and quantification of aortic valve hinge points throughout the cardiac cycle. Utilizing a two-step 3D Unet++ convolutional neural network, the model processes high-resolution Computed Tomography (CT) images to identify hinge points which can be used subsequently to estimate proper prosthetic valve sizing. Although the first step in the segmentation of region of interest (ROI) achieve high accuracy, the second step in detecting hinge coordinates can be further refined to improve the errors of Euclidean distance and angle between predicted plane and ground-truth plane.

articleTitle: Effectiveness of Profiling-based Sketch Configuration: a Measurement Study
abstract: Network management relies on measuring a broad array of traffic metrics via the data plane for operational tasks (e.g., traffic engineering, attack detection, anomaly detection, and workload profiling). To collect each desired metric with a low data plane resource footprint, sketches have emerged as an attractive option. Sketch algorithms are sensitive to resource allocation, but existing methods for configuring sketch resources are not comprehensive. Some are not general enough, and others involve high computational costs. Moreover, when a network operator has diverse measurement tasks, these methods often only consider individual metrics and do not consider an ensemble of metrics. The profiling-based method can serve as an alternative approach to resource configuration, offering advantages such as generality, cost-effectiveness, and feasibility for an ensemble of metrics. However, due to the uncertainties introduced by network dynamics, the reliability of profiling-based measurements is still an important issue worth exploring. The goal of this paper is to conduct an extensive measurement study that evaluates the effectiveness of profiling-based sketch configuration. We observe from our measurement analysis that profiling-based configuration is practical and efficient as it is reliable even when traffic patterns change. We further identify a few challenging scenarios that need to adapt configurations to the proper profiles of varying traffic patterns.

articleTitle: Paired-domination Problem on Circle and k-polygon Graphs
abstract: A vertex set D ⊆ V is considered a dominating set of G if every vertex in V − D is adjacent to at least one vertex in D. We called a dominating set D as a paired-dominating set if the subgraph of G induced by D contains a perfect matching. In this paper, we show that determining the minimum paired-dominating set on circle graphs is NP-complete. We further propose an $O\left( {n{{\left( {\frac{n}{{{k^2} - k}}} \right)}^{2{k^2} - 2k}}} \right)$-time algorithm for k-polygon graphs, a subclass of circle graphs, for finding the minimum paired-dominating set. Moreover, we extend our method to improve the algorithm for finding the minimum dominating set on k-polygon graphs in [E.S. Elmallah and L.K. Stewart, Independence and domination in polygon graphs, Discrete Appl. Math., 1993] and reduce their time-complexity from $O\left( {{n^{4{k^2} + 3}}} \right)$ to $O\left( {n{{\left( {\frac{n}{{{k^2} - k}}} \right)}^{2{k^2} - 4k}}} \right)$.

articleTitle: Car Lane and River Bank Detection through Ensemble Learning
abstract: In this study, we propose a novel approach to enhance edge detection for car lane and river bank detection through ensemble learning. We developed a refined version of the UNet model, named UNet refinement, and combined it with Restormer and ZoomNet models, each trained in different environments, to predict edge images. The predictions were integrated using a voting-based ensemble learning method. This study highlights the effectiveness of ensemble learning and our UNet refinement module in improving the performance of individual models for complex image processing tasks related to car lane and river bank detection.

articleTitle: HDRMamba: High Dynamic Range Video Reconstruction Based on State Space Models
abstract: High dynamic range (HDR) video reconstruction remains a challenging task, particularly when dealing with dynamic scenes and moving objects, which can easily cause ghosting artifacts. While recent deep learning approaches have demonstrated possess deghosting capabilities, they often struggle with computational efficiency. In this work, we present HDRMamba, an architecture designed to address these limitations by leveraging State Space Models. Our method adopts an improved Mamba architecture, incorporating both spatial and temporal scanning mechanisms, which enable more efficient modeling of long-range dependencies across multiple frames while maintaining linear computational complexity. Additionally, we propose a prompt-tuning method that allows the model to adjust its features based on the exposure level of the input reference frame. Experimental results demonstrate that HDRMamba offers a solution that balances performance with efficient computation, making it a promising solution for real-world HDR video applications.

articleTitle: Two Edge-Disjoint Hamiltonian Cycles in Shuffle-cubes
abstract: The n-dimensional shuffle-cube SQ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf>, a variation of the hypercube Q<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf>, has the same number of vertices and the same number of edges as Q<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf>, but it has only about 1/4 of the diameter of Q<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf>. In the interconnection network, some efficient communication algorithms can be designed based on Hamiltonian cycles. In addition, two edge-disjoint Hamiltonian cycles also provide the edge-fault tolerant Hamiltonicity. In this paper, we show two edge-disjoint Hamiltonian cycles in SQ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf>, and then provide two algorithms to construct these cycles. Finally, we give recursive constructions of two edge-disjoint Hamiltonian cycles in SQ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf> for n ≥ 6.

articleTitle: Enhancing Image Recognition Using Hierarchical Neural Networks Tree in Computer Vision
abstract: Image classification is an important research direction in the field of artificial intelligence and machine learning. However, it faces substantial challenges when dealing with visually similar items that possess different characteristics. To address this issue, this article proposes a low redundancy with acceptable accuracy classification method with data augmentation and modularity of neural networks using a Hierarchical Neural Network Tree (HNN-Tree). This method can accurately distinguish between visually similar items with different characteristics, aiming to improve task management and efficiency. Our approach integrates Augmentplus to do image augmentation to enhance the image and mean softmax likelihood to classify super cluster reducing the complexity. The models were trained and validated on the datasets Flower-102 and Food-101, achieving test error of 0.012 and 0.082, respectively. Compared to other artificial intelligence in image classification methods, our work demonstrates acceptable result test error but with a minimal number of parameters in image classification tasks.

articleTitle: Using AI to identify patients in Smart Healthcare
abstract: Objectives: The Taiwan Ministry of Health and Welfare advocates for hospitals to implement patient identification processes, and the Joint Commission on Accreditation of Healthcare Organizations in the United States also mandates positive patient identification. However, investigations have found that 16.5% of hospitals have not implemented these processes, impacting patient safety.Methods: Artificial intelligence (AI) excels at image recognition and can automatically verify patients. From April to June 2024, nine wards in a school-affiliated hospital were selected to establish an environment for physiological data transmission using near field communication (NFC) for patient identification and data transfer.Results: Based on the confusion matrix, the recognition precision is 86.7%, the recall is 72.2%, the model accuracy is 92.6%, and Net Promoter Score (NPS) is 84. Each nurse saved an average of 4.8 minutes in measuring vital signs electronically compared to traditional methods (p = .043).Conclusions: Our findings suggest that AI, combined with NFC technology, can play a significant role in shaping the future of healthcare.

articleTitle: Adaptive Access Gateway Function Framework with P4 Accelerated User Plane
abstract: In order to facilitate the 5G Wireless and Wireline Convergence (5G-WWC) architecture, the Access Gateway Function (AGF) is defined as an interworking function between the 5G core (5GC) and fixed network residential gateways (FN-RG), utilizing a non-3GPP wireline access network. As a proxy, AGF enables communication between the FN-RG and the 5GC. This paper presents an adaptive architecture integrating different access gateway functional user planes. We have implemented a P4 switch-accelerated access gateway user plane with data stream bandwidth management to verify the functionality and adaptability of the adaptive architecture.

articleTitle: CBW: Reducing Data Write Back with Circular Bubble Write for DM-SMR Disks
abstract: As the demand for storage capacity continues to rise, Shingled Magnetic Recording (SMR) disks promise higher storage density through the overlapping of adjacent tracks. However, the sequential write constraint inherent in SMR could result in increased latency during write operations. To balance performance and cost, a portion of SMR storage is used as a persistent cache (PC), employing a log-structured method to enhance write speed. When the PC is full, a garbage collection (GC) policy migrates valid data to the native data area (NDA), freeing up space. However, inefficient data migration can occur if access frequency is not considered, leading to unnecessary writes. To address this issue, we propose the Circular Bubble Write (CBW) scheme, which divides the PC into four areas (including rookie area, rookie buffer, hot area, and cold area) and adaptively places data based on access frequency. This ensures hot data remains in the PC while only cold data migrates to the NDA. The experiment results showed that the CBW scheme could reduce average response time by up to 84% and unnecessary write-backs by up to 95% in write-intensive workloads.

articleTitle: OVS-DPDK-I: A CPU-Efficient High-Speed Open vSwitch
abstract: As cloud computing has prospered, more and more demands and usage scenarios have emerged. So, a robust resource allocation strategy is urgently needed. Usually, a physical server runs many virtual machines (VMs), and the switch allows these VMs to communicate over the Internet. Open vSwitch (OVS) is one of the most popular virtual switches. Besides, there is an accelerated version: OVS-DPDK, which can achieve 5 times throughput than vanilla OVS, but requires more CPUs. When launching the VMs, the operator must choose to configure OVS or OVS-DPDK according to the requirements of the network. However, those have some disadvantages, so we propose an enhanced OVS based on OVS-DPDK, which is named OVS-DPDK-I. The test results show that our technique can transfer packets as fast as OVS-DPDK, and when the transmission rate is low, CPU utilization can be 50% lower than OVS-DPDK, even lower than OVS. In terms of CPU utilization, we also monitor network latency and explain how network traffic patterns affect it.

articleTitle: A Narrative Ethics Education Website Develop: From Design Thinking to Action Research
abstract: The decision-making process in breast cancer care presents emotional challenges, influencing patients and professionals, particularly in complex treatment scenarios. Healthcare providers face numerous ethical challenges in patient care and treatment decision-making, significantly impacting clinical practice. Consequently, ethics education is crucial in medical and nursing training programs. Integrating ethical concepts, codes, and reflection into nursing curricula helps students navigate moral dilemmas in clinical settings. The COVID-19 pandemic has accelerated the adoption of online learning, offering flexibility and overcoming spatial barriers. This study employs design thinking and action research to develop an ethical narrative website for breast cancer education. The curriculum aims to deepen understanding of moral and emotional and l issues and decision-making in breast surgery among nursing students, emphasizing patient perspectives and support.

articleTitle: A Study on Reinforcement Learning in Tri-Othello
abstract: The game of Tri-Othello is a newly designed three-player board game inspired by Othello. This paper modifies the rules of Tri-Othello to reduce the learning curve for human players while maintaining its fun and fairness. We implemented a game-playing program using reinforcement learning with the revised rules and compared its playing strength with a version based on the max<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</sup> search algorithm. Our experimental results showed that the trained reinforcement learning model performed better than the max<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</sup>-based program.

articleTitle: Journey to Zero-X: Enabling Autonomous Self-Management Framework in Private 5G Networks
abstract: Since 2023, there has been a trend towards emphasizing network control, especially among large enterprises seeking to improve internal autonomy. This paper outlines a self-management framework designed to enable autonomous management in private 5G networks. Our framework addresses manual management challenges by incorporating four essential capabilities: self-configuration to enhance connectivity quality, self-optimization to improve streaming performance, self-healing for expedited obstacle resolution, and self-protection to ensure network security. By employing this framework, we establish an autonomous network within private 5G networks, providing users with a Zero-X experience.

articleTitle: Disturbance Insertion for Improving Quantum and GPU Annealer Performance
abstract: This paper investigates the impact of introducing disturbances into quadratic unconstrained binary optimization (QUBO) formulas to enhance the performance of both the quantum annealer (QA) and the GPU annealer (GPUA). We propose a disturbance insertion method to insert into QUBO formula coefficients some disturbances that are parameterized by the insertion ratio, Gaussian distribution mean, and standard deviation. By applying the proposed method to a QA (viz., the D-Wave Advantage annealer) and a GPUA (viz., the Compal Quantix solver) for solving two well-known combinatorial optimization problems, the traveling salesperson problem and the 0/1 knapsack problem, we identify appropriate disturbance parameters that facilitate the annealing process for better solving the two problems.

articleTitle: Provisioning a Reliable Kubernetes cluster with CI/CD
abstract: In today’s fast-paced IT environment, adopting Infrastructure-as-Code mechanisms to automate the provisioning of servers, virtual machines, and Kubernetes clusters has become essential. However, relying solely on IaC mechanisms can result in issues such as package versions, configuration errors, and manual script modifications leading to provisioning failures and wasted time. This study introduces the CSIT Golden IaC Framework at the Computer Science Information Technologies Center of National Yang Ming Chiao Tung University, which combines Golden Images with existing IaC scripts and integrates Continuous Integration/Continuous Delivery mechanisms to ensure rapid and reliable provisioning of identical environments. Experimental results show significant time savings and error reduction, paving the way for automated management of Kubernetes clusters.

articleTitle: Enhancing the Performance of Virtual State Channel Establishment with Smart Contract of Blockchain
abstract: Since Bitcoin was first invented in 2008, blockchains have gradually gained public attention. However, as a global payment infrastructure, Bitcoin is extremely slow compared to traditional payment services such as PayPal and Visa. Even today, more than ten years after the emergence of Bitcoin, only a minority of people use it as a daily payment method. One of the reasons attributed to the low popularity of Bitcoin is the slowness of blockchains. Therefore, how to speed up blockchains has become a popular research topic. Among various solutions, the state channel, which processes numerous transactions outside of the main blockchain, is the most promising one. In this paper, we propose a broadcast strategy to speed up the construction process of virtual state channels that build upon state channels by using smart contracts. Moreover, we use the leader election method to ensure data consistency between two nodes in order to solve possible deadlock and race condition situations without breaking the security characteristic of the virtual state channel. According to our experiment result, the proposed strategy yields more than two times speedup on average and also achieves 50% speedup in terms of throughput when using asynchronous operation.

articleTitle: Combining EMR rankings for multi-image queries
abstract: In CBIR (Content-Based Image Retrieval), using a single query often leads to limitations in semantic image search. The Efficient Manifold Ranking (EMR) algorithm has been widely used in CBIR and often uses low-level or high-level features for image querying. However, high-level features from Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) have more advantages, helping to describe the semantics of images more clearly than low-level features such as color, texture, and shape.To improve the performance of the EMR-based image retrieval algorithm in content-based image querying, this study proposes a method to combine the rankings of each query image. Instead of relying on only a single query image, we combine the EMR ranking results of two input query images into a single ranking. This method helps to increase the accuracy and efficiency of querying by leveraging information from different perspectives of semantics.Experiments were conducted on the VGG60K dataset to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed ranking method in improving the quality of image retrieval.

articleTitle: Multi-Argument Fuzzing by Reinforcement Learning
abstract: Fuzzing is a popular technique for testing software quality. This paper proposes a method to apply reinforcement learning to multi-argument fuzzing test. By tracking the rewards of each parameter to solve the MAB (Multi-Armed Bandit) problem of multi-argument selection and by using the average value of the total number of new paths and new crashes to determine the selection of exploration and exploitation stages, we can achieve a balance between these two stages to obtain the maximum reward.By this method, this paper implements a fuzzing test tool called MARL. In terms of edge coverage, the binary vim performed best, with MARL achieving 24.31 times higher coverage than MOPT and 14.27 times higher than AFL. Among the unique crashes, the binary nm-new performed best. Within the time limit, only MARL triggered 4 crashes, while the other fuzzers did not trigger any crashes.

articleTitle: Exploring Automated Frequency Coordination System for 6 GHz Wi-Fi in Taiwan
abstract: Federal Communications Commission (FCC) opens the usage of the 6 GHz frequency band for Wi-Fi to accommodate the growing service demands. To better coordinate the licensed services, the Automatic Frequency Coordination (AFC) system is developed so that Wi-Fi can utilize the available channels over the 6 GHz frequency band for service delivery without interfering with the existing licensed services. In this paper, we investigate and resolve the challenge of deploying the AFC system in Taiwan via the Open AFC project. Specifically, a data format conversion procedure is proposed to integrate Taiwan’s available terrain data into the AFC system. Current results not only show the compatibility and precision of the conversion but also illustrate the possibility of deploying the AFC system for Wi-Fi 6E/7 in Taiwan.

articleTitle: Deep Learning Approaches with Attention Mechanisms for Go Strength Imitation and Style Recognition
abstract: With the advancement of AI technology, imitating human intelligence and endowing machines with personalities have become crucial research areas. This study aims to enhance the performance of Go AI through techniques such as CNN, ResNet, and attention mechanisms, mimicking different levels of playing strength and imitating machines with unique play styles. This research focuses on the algorithms and model architectures for strength imitation and play style recognition in Go. Factors such as move order, board state, and liberties are considered for strength imitation, employing CNN with residual blocks, and introducing Channel Attention and Spatial Attention mechanisms. For play style recognition, a similar model architecture is used with the addition of Spatial Dropout to prevent overfitting. The results show that incorporating liberties as input yields better performance in strength imitation and play style recognition. The final model achieved approximately 56% accuracy in strength imitation with a Top-5 accuracy of 86% and 82% accuracy in play style recognition.

articleTitle: CAA-Net: Class-Aware Attention Network for Selective Target Label Salient Object Detection
abstract: This paper aims to accomplish salient-object detection (SOD) by considering a selective-focus object class. In realistic applications of saliency prediction, people may focus on a particular class of objects. Few studies consider both objectives simultaneously to achieve the requirements for the above applications. Thus, we propose a novel class-aware SOD network that predicts salient objects within the specific class of human interest. Experiments reveal that the proposed network can effectively predict salient objects of the selected target class and can be applied to other saliency-based applications.

articleTitle: Frequency based Semantic Consistency Groups in Object Detection
abstract: This paper presents the results of applying semantic knowledge to object detection using deep learning. We discover semantic relationships between groups of objects by counting co-occurrence frequencies of object groups before combining them with detection output from Faster R-CNN network in a re-optimization process for better detection. The research was conducted on two datasets – MS COCO and a small self-made dataset consisting of images of beverage items on shelves in several supermarkets.

articleTitle: Artificial intelligence technology for automatic segmentation of lymphatic areas in radiotherapy for pelvic tumors
abstract: The clinical treatments of pelvic cancers, such as cervical cancer, adenocarcinoma, and prostate cancer, include not only surgical resection but also radiotherapy. Radiotherapy uses radiation to target and control the development of the disease. Before radiotherapy, precise marking and delineation are essential for radiation dose planning. The delineated areas include the lesion site and clinically determined potential areas, such as lymph nodes and surrounding organs at risk (OAR), including the bladder, uterus, large intestine, and small intestine. Currently, the clinical labeling of these lesions and OAR areas is done manually by experienced radiation oncologists and medical physicists. The pelvic cavity's anatomical structure is complex, and the lymph node area in the pelvic cavity is recognized as a high-risk area, thus included in the irradiation area. However, lymph nodes on CT images have fewer clear borders than other OAR areas, making it difficult to delineate and increasing variability between different markers. This study employs artificial intelligence algorithms to automatically delineate clinical target volumes (CTV), especially pelvic lymph nodes, and attempts to incorporate anatomical information to facilitate more accurate annotation. This approach aims to reduce the burden of clinical treatment planning and improve precision in radiotherapy.

articleTitle: An Enhancement on Fault Detection for Imbalanced Data in Industrial Chiller Systems
abstract: In many industrial control settings of smart manufacturing industries, Heating, Ventilation, and Air Conditioning (HVAC) systems are essential for maintaining a stable environment that meets production requirements. Among these systems, chillers consume the most energy, making energy efficiency management of chiller units a crucial research topic to date. However, research in this area often faces a shortage of sample data for anomalies, leading to an imbalance in the number of samples between normal and abnormal data in modeling fault detection. This imbalance can result in biased judgments by classifiers. Therefore, this paper will compare the use of oversampling combined with undersampling to address imbalanced data with the use of Generative Adversarial Network (GAN) to generate realistic abnormal data, aiming to mitigate the issue of imbalanced data. The experimental results demonstrate that compared to oversampling and undersampling, GAN can effectively generate diverse abnormal data, enabling classifiers to achieve excellent modeling results.

articleTitle: Automatic Bridge Bidding Model Based on LSTM and Deep Reinforcement Learning
abstract: There are two phases for playing bridge: bidding and playing. We focus on the bidding phase, which is critical for information exchange. Yeh and Lin have designed a deep reinforcement learning bidding model, but this model has a significant non-competitive assumption -- the opponent always bids PASS. We remove this limitation to reflect actual bidding situations. Unlike previous methods in the literature, we use a Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) model specialized for time series data combined with reinforcement learning, which allows the model to learn independently without relying on human bridge games for training. We also combine probability simulation and upper confidence bounds to choose bidding actions. Experiments show that our approach achieves an average cost of 4.56, outperforming Yeh and Lin's approach without the bidding limitation.

articleTitle: Social Temperature: Real-Time Social Activity Monitoring Based on Deep Learning Methods
abstract: In the study, the social temperature model for measuring social activity of a space first proposed. From observations of crowd (number of people), group atmosphere (positive or negative emotion), and social interaction (conversation), the social temperature model quantizes social activity to the value of social temperature in the range of 0 to 40 degrees Celsius. A real-time camera monitoring system has developed based on deep learning methods to detect motion, human face and identity, face expression and talking voice, and provides an unconstrained social activity monitoring. Deep learning methods of GMM model, YOLOv8n model, Dlib model and Deepface model were adopted in motion detection, face detection, human identification recognition and face expression recognition, respectively. In addition, the OpenAI Whisper-small model was applied in Speech-to-Text conversion to retrieve texts data from audio signals, and Voice Activity Detector run in local devices for distinguishing speech from ambient noise of environments. For real-time computation, a GPU server was built to transfer images and voices from local devices of users via FastAPI. The system has been applied in various authentic contexts including office, school and home scenarios. The contribution of the work provides an objective way for measuring social activity of people and the belonging space in mental aspect that tries to arise people the awareness of their social states with others.

articleTitle: A Survey on Constellation Routing Methods in 6G Non-Terrestrial Networks
abstract: In the era of 6G, Non-Terrestrial Networks (NTNs) are gaining attention due to their potential to provide global coverage and enhanced connectivity. This survey explores the diverse routing methods employed in NTN constellations, focusing on centralized, distributed, and hybrid approaches. Centralized routing, incorporating AI control layers and reinforcement learning, offers global optimization, reducing latency and packet loss. Distributed routing methods like LCO-RIP and ADR address link congestion and enhance flexibility and responsiveness in dynamic environments. Hybrid routing strategies, exemplified by MaCRo and SDMCN architectures, integrate the advantages of centralized and distributed methods, optimizing data transmission and reliability. Evaluations based on parameters like end-to-end delay, packet loss rate, and throughput highlight the effectiveness of these routing strategies. The survey underscores the significant achievements in improving network performance and reliability, providing a comprehensive foundation for the efficient operation of NTN constellation systems in 6G networks.

articleTitle: Graph-Based Temporal Attention for Coronary Artery Disease Prediction Using Electronic Health Records
abstract: Deep learning has significantly enhanced the ability to predict health outcomes using Electronic Health Records (EHR). However, the challenges posed by EHR data, such as sparsity, heterogeneity, and temporal complexity, necessitate innovative representation techniques. This research introduces a novel graph-based approach to effectively represent EHR data for the early prediction of coronary artery disease (CAD). We proposed a dual-graph approach by constructing then fusing two distinct graphs: a diagnosis graph and a lab graph. The diagnosis graph employs diagnosis nodes and visit nodes to capture patient diagnoses over time, while the lab graph discretizes continuous laboratory measurement results into four quantile levels, represented as lab nodes connected to visit nodes. Graph convolutional networks (GCN) are used separately on each graph to manage data sparsity, and a time-aware transformer layer captures the temporal dynamics of patient visits. The resulting visit embeddings from both graphs are concatenated and processed through fully connected layers for dimensionality reduction and final classification. Our model was evaluated on a dataset of 6,272 CAD patients and 47,295 non-CAD patients, using three different observation periods. Ablation studies were also performed to assess the impact of using only diagnosis data or only laboratory measurement data. The results demonstrate that our dual-graph approach effectively integrates diagnosis and laboratory measurement data, capturing both spatial and temporal information to accurately predict CAD, achieving a best AUROC (area under the receiver operation characteristic) of 0.908 ± 0.008. This method simplifies the graph structure, enhances interpretability, and improves predictive performance compared to previous techniques.

articleTitle: An Integrated Questionnaire Survey Method Utilizing Cloud Services and Communication Platforms: Enhancing Research Efficiency in Healthcare Settings
abstract: Questionnaire surveys are a common data collection method in nursing research, but traditional research methods face challenges such as low efficiency and inconsistent data quality. This study proposes a Platform-integrated Real-time Intelligent Survey Model (PRISM) based on cloud technology and instant messaging platforms. PRISM integrates Google Workspace, LINE Messaging API, and Google Cloud, achieving efficient questionnaire management, real-time data validation, and visualization analysis. In an application at a regional hospital, PRISM reduced data collection time from 30-45 days to 14 days, data processing time from 13.33 hours to 0.5 hours, and research costs from 15,000-20,000 NTD to approximately 10 NTD. PRISM improved data quality through automatic contradiction detection and real-time feedback mechanisms, providing an efficient, low-cost, and high-quality solution for large-scale, multi-stage questionnaire surveys.

articleTitle: Changes in Spontaneous Alpha—Gamma Coupling in Primary Dysmenorrhea
abstract: Women of reproductive age who experience cyclic menstrual pain without pelvic abnormalities are considered primary dysmenorrhea (PDM). While our earlier research discovered the associations between BDNF Val66Met polymorphism and functional changes in the descending pain modulatory systems in PDM, as well as weakened slow/fast interconnections across the menstrual cycle, there is a lack of understanding of how BDNF Val66Met polymorphism influences neural oscillations across the menstrual cycle. This study aimed to address this gap by investigating the effects of gene polymorphism on resting-state oscillations during and after long-term menstrual discomfort. Resting-state magnetoencephalography (MEG) recordings were evaluated for n:m cross-frequency coupling (CFC) in 50 individuals with PDM and 49 healthy women (CON). Psychological assessments and cross-frequency couplings at each menstruation (MENS) and periovulatory (POV) period were compared between BDNF Val66Met gene polymorphisms. The state-anxiety scale for CON with Met/Met was inversely correlated with alpha/gamma phase-phase coupling in the left superior parietal regions during menstruation. In contrast, PDM with Met/Met showed an inverse pattern of n:m CFC couplings. Altered functional coupling in pain-related regions may arise from the interaction between the BDNF Val66Met genotyping and long-term pain experience, ultimately affecting the perception, emotion, and attention to pain in those experiencing cyclic pain.

articleTitle: Advancing Data Privacy in Semiconductor Manufacturing: Thumbnail Preserving Encryption for CycleGAN-Processed Wafer Images
abstract: Given the limited availability of defective wafer images on actual production lines, there are challenges associated with time constraints in their collection. To address the data imbalance issue concerning defect modes in wafer images, we utilize CycleGAN deep learning networks to devise a defect mode generation solution. Due to the risk of hardware damage, we store the generated wafer images in the cloud and employ an scheme similar to thumbnail preserving encryption to achieve a balance between privacy and security by presenting ciphertext in a low-resolution version of plaintext. This approach aims to provide user accessibility while enhancing automated production efficiency through an increased number of training samples for defect modes. The obtained results indicate a high resemblance between the generated defective wafer images and authentic defective wafer images. Furthermore, we compute the Peak Signal-to-Noise Ratio of the generated defective wafer images under various TPE schemes to assess their security. Experimental results demonstrate that the generated wafer images exhibit lower PSNR values and higher security under the R-LSB scheme.

articleTitle: WiFi CSI-based Fall Detection from Wearable Devices
abstract: As the population ages, falls increasingly pose a significant public health concern. This has led to the proposal of many fall detection methods. Some of these methods, based on Wi-Fi Channel State Information (CSI), offer a cost-effective alternative that protects user privacy, which may be compromised by some vision-based solutions. However, conventional CSI-based methods have a major limitation: both the Wi-Fi transmitter and receiver are statically deployed, and only users located within the range between them can be detected. To address this, we propose a solution where detection is based on users’ wearable devices, which send Wi-Fi data to the AP, and the AP collects CSI data for fall detection. We first conduct a case study to confirm its feasibility by considering both time and frequency-time domain features extracted from CSI data. We then apply two spectrogram-based CSI methods, image recognition and features classification on spectrograms. Practical evaluation shows their effectiveness with commercial off-the-shelf (COTS) devices, including Wi-Fi NIC and smartwatch. In particular, the image recognition method can achieve accuracy higher than 80% in most cases with mobile wearable devices.

articleTitle: Analysis of DNA Methylation Biomarkers through Liquid Biopsies for Early Breast Cancer Detection
abstract: According to World Health Organization (WHO) and World Cancer Research Fund International (WCRF International), breast cancer has become the most common cancer globally, significantly impacting women's health. This study utilized GDC and GEO public methylation chip datasets from breast cancer patients. Combined with comorbidity data analysis of these patients, critical biomarkers were identified through analyzing differential expression levels of methylation loci, serving as indicators for breast cancer risk assessment. Gene Ontology (GO) functional annotations were applied for hierarchical clustering. Functional similarities between any two genetic loci were evaluated based on their annotated GO terms, enabling the observation of candidate biomarker relationships for diagnosis biomarker selection. Furthermore, by integrating Boruta for feature selection and applying Recursive Feature Elimination (RFE) to evaluate the performance of various machine learning models, the optimal methylation biomarker combinations for breast cancer detection could be identified. The results identified eight important DNA methylation biomarkers, including CMTM5, PDCD1LG2, MIR124-3, NEFM, PTF1A, CX3CL1, PCYT2, and KCNE3 as important biomarker candidates. After functional clustering analysis, these markers exhibited excellent performance with three biomarker combinations for both tissue and liquid samples from breast cancer patients, with average prediction accuracies ranging from 0.91 to 0.93 for tissue samples and from 0.71 to 0.76 for liquid samples. Early observation of methylation differences from the suggested breast cancer biomarkers could prevent tumor formation and reduce the risk of surgical operations by early precision diagnosis and treatment.

articleTitle: Smart Handover between 5G and Wi-Fi over QUIC at Network Edge for Maximizing Throughput
abstract: Multi-access edge computing (MEC) and heterogeneous access networks are critical technologies in modern 5G communication system. MEC deploys application services near base stations, while heterogeneous networks provide multiple access network, such as 5G cellular, and Wi-Fi. Additionally, edge applications can directly collect relevant information from the radio access network to optimize performance and fulfill stringent requirements in term of bandwidth and latency. However, the default configuration of mobile devices prioritizes Wi-Fi as the primary interface to avoid cellular billing, which can degrade throughput in areas with poor Wi-Fi signal strength. To address this issue, we propose a smart handover decision-making framework that facilitates cooperation between the user equipment (UE), access network, and MEC to estimate throughput for handover decisions. By employing a deep reinforcement learning model, the framework learns the difference between estimated and actual throughput, enabling dynamic selection of the best-performing access network, whether 5G or Wi-Fi. Our trained model also supports online learning, allowing it to adapt to changing environments. Experimental results demonstrate that our approach achieves, on average, over 96% of optimal throughput in various environments, with network selection accuracy ranging from 88.52% to 92.72%.

articleTitle: Enhanced Taint Inference for Directed Fuzzing
abstract: In recent years, fuzzing has become a well-known automated testing tool. Although fast execution speed, fuzzing does not have information about the program state and data flow such that it cannot meet more complex branch conditions and extend the program coverage in depth. If fuzzing can introduce the technology of taint analysis, the input portion that dominates the branch conditions will be obtained. Mutation operations specifically targeting critical bytes can significantly reduce the input length and quantity used for testing and improve the ability to pass complex branch conditions. There are two challenges that must be overcome when applying a taint analysis. First, excessive time seriously affects the execution speed of fuzzing; second, strict execution environment requirements will limit the application scope of fuzzing. Taint inference was the first to be proposed as a solution with faster execution speed and lower execution environment requirements, using corresponding mutation strategies to generate effective test inputs, allowing program execution to penetrate into more complex branches.The feasibility of introducing taint inference into directed fuzzing is verified preliminarily. The results show that Saryn(Go) can indeed reach program locations that are difficult to reach with other fuzzing tools. In addition, it can be used only for branch conditions that must be passed to reach the target program position and have not yet been passed, not for branches that cannot reach the target program position or have been satisfied, alleviating the overhead caused by taint inference and thereby increasing the efficiency of directed fuzzing.

articleTitle: A Deep Learning for Predicting Possibility of Bluetooth Low Energy Tag Signals
abstract: With the rapid growth of IoT technology, using Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) gateways to track the trajectory of elderly individuals can help prevent them from getting lost. However, BLE tag signals do not persist, and BLE gateways often enter standby mode for extended periods, resulting in unnecessary energy waste and reducing the lifespan of the devices. To address this issue, predicting the likelihood of BLE tag signals is essential to conserve energy. This paper presents a deep learning approach to enhance the operational efficiency and lifespan of BLE gateways deployed in an IoT system. The system consists of two major modules: the Number of BLE Tags Estimation Module and the Next Accessed BLE Gateway Prediction Module. The Number of BLE Tags Estimation Module leverages a CNN-GRU (Convolutional Neural Network - Gated Recurrent Unit) architecture to predict the time lapse between the sensing of signals from BLE tags. The Next Accessed BLE Gateway Prediction Module employs a self-attention mechanism to predict which specific BLE gateway will receive the BLE tag signal, further optimizing system performance. Experimental results show that the proposed prediction model effectively reduces unnecessary energy consumption, thereby improving the efficiency and service life of the entire IoT system.

articleTitle: Learning Cross-domain Keypoint Detection between Image and Point Cloud with Auxiliary Depth Scan Map
abstract: 2D-3D cross-domain registration is the process of finding a geometry transformation aligning a 2D image and 3D point cloud to a consistent coordinate. That is, we finding the camera pose, i.e., the extrinsic of the imaging camera is the frame among the coordinate of given 3D point cloud. With the retrieve pose, we conduct various real-world applications like Augmented Reality and the localization of autonomous driving vehicles/robots. In this study, we propose geometry-aware 2D-3D cross domain keypoint detection (GCD). This is a novel approach for 2D-3D cross-domain-keypoint detection that applies a dual-branch network to predict the detection uncertainty score for each point in 2D and 3D inputs. The key to cross-domain detection is the intrinsic divergence between a 2D RGB image and a 3D geometry point cloud. Hence, we propose to exploit the dense map of 2D images in our training process to bridge the gap between the two modalities.

articleTitle: CNN Inference Workload Distribution Considering Accumulative Effect of Receptive Fields
abstract: Operating an artificial intelligence and machine learning (AI/ML) model requires significant computing power, posing a substantial challenge for edge devices with limited resources. A potential way to accelerate the operations is to distribute the workload to multiple collaborative devices. For the inference using a convolutional neural network (CNN), the workload distributed is complicated by the overlapping input tensors among workers due to the accumulative effect of receptive fields (AERF). This factor incurs extra communication time, which was overlooked by prior studies. In this paper, we propose an approach to CNN inference time minimization by aggregating the inference workload distributed to multiple heterogeneous computing devices. Our result shows a 10% speed-up against the benchmark.
